{{short description|Italian mathematician}}
[[File:Vezzosi toen.jpg|thumb|Gabriele Vezzosi and Bertrand Toen, Oberwolfach 2002]]
'''Gabriele Vezzosi''' is an Italian mathematician, born in Florence, Italy. His main interest is [[algebraic geometry]].

Vezzosi earned an MS degree in Physics at the [[University of Florence]], under the supervision of [[Alexandre Mikhailovich Vinogradov|Alexandre M. Vinogradov]], and a PhD in Mathematics at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore]] in [[Pisa]], under the supervision of [[Angelo Vistoli]]. His first papers dealt with [[differential calculus]] over [[commutative ring]]s, [[intersection theory]], ([[equivariant algebraic K-theory|equivariant]]) algebraic [[K-theory]], [[motivic homotopy theory]], and existence of [[vector bundles]] on singular [[algebraic surface]]s.

Around 2001–2002 he started his collaboration with [[Bertrand Toën]]. Together, they created [[homotopical algebraic geometry]] (HAG),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Toën|first1=Bertrand|author1-link=Bertrand Toën |last2=Vezzosi|first2=Gabriele |title=Homotopical algebraic geometry I: topos theory|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|date=2005|volume=193|issue=2|pages=257–372 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2004.05.004|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0207028|s2cid=119131806}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Toën|first1=Bertrand|author1-link=Bertrand Toën | last2=Vezzosi|first2=Gabriele|title=HAG II|journal=[[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]]|date=2008|volume=193|issue=902|pages=1–228}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=ncatlab entry: Homotopical Algebraic Geometry|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/homotopical+algebraic+geometry |website=ncatlab |access-date=February 10, 2018}}</ref> whose more relevant part is [[derived algebraic geometry]] (DAG),<ref>{{cite web|title=ncatlab entry: Derived Algebraic Geometry|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/derived+algebraic+geometry|website=ncatlab}}</ref> which is by now a powerful and widespread theory.<ref>{{cite web|title=Harvard DAG learning seminar|url=http://people.fas.harvard.edu/~amathew/dag.html |access-date=February 10, 2018}}</ref><ref name="MSRI">{{cite web|last1=MSRI|title=Program "Derived Algebraic Geometry"|url=https://www.msri.org/programs/306|website=MSRI|access-date=April 19, 2018}}</ref> Slightly later, this theory was reconsidered, and highly expanded by [[Jacob Lurie]].

More recently, Vezzosi together with [[Tony Pantev]], [[Bertrand Toën]] and [[Michel Vaquié]] defined a derived version of symplectic structures<ref>{{cite journal|title=Shifted symplectic structures|journal=[[Publ. Math. IHÉS]]|date=2013|volume=17|issue=1|pages=271–328|doi=10.1007/s10240-013-0054-1|arxiv=1111.3209|last1=Pantev|first1=Tony|last2=Toën|first2=Bertrand|last3=Vaquié|first3=Michel|last4=Vezzosi|first4=Gabriele|s2cid=11246087}}</ref> and studied important properties and examples (an important instance being [[Kai Behrend]]'s [[symmetric obstruction theory|symmetric obstruction theories]]); further together with [[Damien Calaque]] these authors introduced and studied a derived version of [[Poisson manifold|Poisson]] and coisotropic structures<ref>{{cite journal|title=Shifted Poisson structures and deformation quantization|journal=[[Journal of Topology]] |date=2017 |volume=10|issue=2 |pages=483–584 |doi=10.1112/topo.12012|arxiv=1506.03699 |last1=Calaque |first1=Damien |last2=Pantev |first2=Tony |last3=Toën |first3=Bertrand |last4=Vaquié |first4=Michel |last5=Vezzosi |first5=Gabriele |s2cid=117757610 }}</ref> with applications to [[deformation quantization]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Toën|first=Bertrand|author-link=Bertrand Toën|title=Derived algebraic geometry and deformation quantization|url=https://perso.math.univ-toulouse.fr/btoen/files/2012/04/icm2014.pdf|website=ICM-talk (2014)|access-date=February 10, 2018}}</ref>

Lately Toën and Vezzosi (partly in collaboration with Anthony Blanc and Marco Robalo) moved to applications of derived and non-commutative geometry to arithmetic geometry, especially to [[Spencer Bloch]]'s [[conductor conjecture]].<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Blanc|first1=Anthony |last2=Robalo|first2=M.|last3=Toen|first3=B. |last4=Vezzosi |first4=Gabriele|title=Motivic Realizations of Singularity Categories and Vanishing Cycles|year=2016 |eprint=1607.03012 |class=math.AG}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Toën|first1=Bertrand|author1-link=Bertrand Toën|last2=Vezzosi |first2=Gabriele |title=Trace formula for dg-categories and Bloch's conductor conjecture I|year=2017|eprint=1710.05902 |class=math.AG}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Vezzosi|first1=Gabriele|title=Applications of non-commutative algebraic geometry to arithmetic geometry|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JCu_-Hab-DA|website=IHES channel- YouTube|date=15 June 2017 |access-date=April 18, 2018}}</ref>

Vezzosi also defined a derived version of quadratic forms, and in collaboration with Benjamin Hennion and Mauro Porta, proved a very general formal gluing result along non-linear flags<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Hennion |first1=Benjamin|last2=Porta| first2=Mauro|last3=Vezzosi|first3=Gabriele|title=Formal gluing along non-linear flags |year=2016|eprint=1607.04503 |class=math.AG}}</ref> with hints of application to a yet conjectural [[Geometric Langlands program]] for varieties of dimension bigger than 1. Together with Benjamin Antieau, Vezzosi proved a [[Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem]] (HKR) for varieties of dimension ''p'' in [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] p.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Antieau|first1=B.|last2=Vezzosi|first2=G.|title=A remark on the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem in characteristic ''p''|year=2017|eprint=1710.06039 |class=math.AG}}</ref>

In 2015 he organised the Oberwolfach Seminar on Derived Geometry<ref>{{cite web|last1=MFO Seminar |title=MFO Seminar, Derived Geometry|url=https://www.mfo.de/occasion/1548a |website=MFO |access-date=April 18, 2018}}</ref> at the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach]] in Germany, and is an organiser of the one-semester thematic program at [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]] in 2019 on [[Derived algebraic geometry]].<ref name="MSRI"/>

Vezzosi spent his career so far in [[Pisa]], [[Florence]], [[Bologna]] and [[Paris]], has had three PhD students (Schürg, Porta and Melani) and is full professor at the [[University of Florence]] (Italy).
